notes.title: Dev Blog #11 – Celebrating Women’s Day Among the Stars!
notes.content:
Hello there, inmates!

It’s time for our eleventh dev blog, and this one is special for two reasons. First—International Women’s Day is just around the corner, and second—we’re kicking off a special sale for our game Space Prison to celebrate! Today, we won’t be focusing solely on combat or weaponry. Instead, we’d like to shine a light on our philosophy of equality and diversity in the galactic world, as well as share a behind-the-scenes look at how it all works within our Wooden Alien team.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/469a55f4e014bd45264223a9323852c1d46593f7.gif[/img]

[h3]From the Start: Zero Discrimination[/h3]
From our earliest sketches of Space Prison, we knew we wouldn’t define our characters based on gender. In everyday life, we don’t discriminate against people because of their gender or sexual orientation—why would we do that in our game? The main differentiators among characters in Space Prison remain their [b]cosmic race and their personality[/b], not whether they’re male, female, or belong to any other gender identity. We initially wanted to introduce an even wider variety of gender identities and alien species, but the project grew so large that we couldn’t fit everything into our development schedule.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/a2de985cdbebc1c97221589ad4ad095eb27510dd.gif[/img]

[h3]Women, Men, and… Beyond?[/h3]
Pop culture works like Orange Is the New Black showcase the [b]challenges women face in prison[/b], as well as how strong they can become in such an environment. That series is primarily about women in prison—Space Prison, however, did not aim for the same themes. Our galactic prison focuses on survival among aliens and bizarre technologies, not on gender divisions. We knew from the start that we wanted women, men, and all sorts of alien life forms in our correctional facility. Everyone here plays an equally important role, and the only differences that matter are their personalities—and maybe some biological quirks if they’re from a species with extra tentacles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/edf35e18b13155c3aa4bd363bd9df54fb1e05977.gif[/img]

[h3]Body and Identity[/h3]
Our unique [b]body-switching mechanic[/b] in Space Prison lets you assume the form of a different gender—or even a different alien species. Throughout the game, you’ll encounter storylines dealing with personal identity: what if someone doesn’t feel comfortable in their original body? In certain quests, you’ll grapple with the consequences of crossing that line and switching to a completely different body. This serves as our metaphor for gender transition in the real world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/b52b3d7d8b29d789038ab63d806a18e33a8a2b3d.gif[/img]

Moreover, Space Prison celebrates freedom in matters of affection and relationships. Romantic bonds between characters of the same gender are common in our cosmic setting—because after all, who’s going to be shocked by that when you’re surrounded by three-eyed aliens and mechanical cyborgs?

[h3]Equality in the Wooden Alien Team[/h3]
Before we dive back into the depths of interstellar cells, we want to shed some light on our everyday reality. At Wooden Alien, we don’t hire people based on gender or stereotypes. We value[b] skills, creativity, and a willingness [/b]to work in a tight-knit team. Over the last year, our team makeup has been nearly balanced—50% men and 50% women. One of our co-founders and our Art Director is Barbara Wiszyńska-Kubit, whose visionary art concepts shape the unique atmosphere of Space Prison and bring depth and character to our ideas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/50d09bcd2002998c36990ffc4819e72faa1a9d8e.png[/img]
[h3]Women’s Day and a Galactic Sale[/h3]
In honor of Women’s Day, we’re launching a special sale with a [b]40% discount[/b]. If you haven’t yet had the chance to explore our cosmic prison adventures, now is the perfect time to jump in. Enjoy discovering all the secrets of Space Prison, and have a fantastic Women’s Day—no matter whether you’re on Earth or somewhere far, far away!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/b81c5c26254e060527f03581f16b66224f5b93d1.png[/img]
Thank you for your support, and don’t miss out on the sale—or you might find yourself in solitary confinement for a week!

See you behind bars!

The Wooden Alien Team

notes.title: Dev Blog #8 - Turn-based mechanics
notes.content:
Hello there inmates,

Here comes our eighth devblog that will focus on the turn-based mechanics you can find in your journey, or rather, the rules of the prison regarding fight among inmates, contraband and other illegal activities. We are keeping an eye on you, inmate!

[h3]At the beginning[/h3]

Did you know Space Prison initially had real-time combat? The fighting style was brawler-based and focused on dexterity. However, during several playtests, we received clear feedback from players stating that this type of combat didn’t fit well with the rest of the game’s mechanics. The players themselves told us that they would much prefer turn-based battles in the prison setting, and so we did!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/a81de437f7c6e52efbf03d722712b234e7e0581b.gif[/img]

We sat down and started by creating a paper prototype of the combat system. From the beginning, we wanted it to have a few core principles – it needed to be[b] simple at its core, enjoyable to execute, and offer the potential for deep development[/b]. So the first four things we locked in were:
[list]
[*] Small spaces
[*] Fast brawls
[*] Skills coming mainly from Gear
[*] Party based
[/list]
We added a few principles to better reflect the setting. We wanted to capture the[b] claustrophobia of the prison[/b], with its tight corridors and rooms on the space station, so we limited the arena to a grid of a [b]maximum size of 6x3[/b]. Some players would prefer a larger combat field, but that’s not the point of short, intense skirmishes in the prison.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/ce078ddabd2df6d85ab9dab95e15c9d227e34155.jpg[/img]
[h3]Hand-Crafted Gear [/h3]

We wanted the combat system to be as well-integrated with the other systems of the game as possible. After all, it’s the element that tests the player’s challenge, and other gameplay elements feed into it. Naturally, one of the most important limitations in prison is the ban on possessions, which is why [b]crafting contraband[/b] plays such a crucial role. The primary items crafted by prisoners are weapons. Among them, there are various types of weapons in four basic categories: knuckles, shivs, whips, and blunts. Each category has its advantages. For example, whips can pull enemies closer, shivs are faster, allowing for quicker attacks and applying bleed effects, and blunt weapons can deal damage to multiple enemies at once.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/de234e92f76eebdfb23ea1d5c12e425532abbd5d.gif[/img]

Besides weapons, there’s an entire arsenal of armor and other protective gear, as well as countless utility items, ranging from simple tools like ropes or throwing knives, to grenades, pills that enhance prisoners' abilities, and even combat drones.

[h3]Team-Based Brawls[/h3]

Speaking of drones, I have to mention our party members. Among the prisoners (and players!) we have supporters of more natural companions, like [b]rats[/b], but also [b]drones[/b] crafted by prisoners at their illegal crafting benches. Both types can be upgraded and equipped with various gear (eg. rat capes or tiny claws for your furry friends). Speaking of upgrade and crafting, spoiler alert : [spoiler] You can also get a Mech Rat ![/spoiler]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/60d92f98ace445654b683625f6c409f1bcb3e160.png[/img]
However, the most important members of the party are the other prisoners. They can make the biggest difference in a fight. Every prisoner has their own set of special strengths and weaknesses. You can discover these to determine which prisoners suit you best depending on the combat.

Of course, none of them will join our side just because we want them to. First, we need to earn their trust and respect. And to do that, it's best to get closer to them and help with their personal issues. Everyone here has a goal, something they want to accomplish.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/c9683ad6de268b3b83d29736c10b798c03370558.gif[/img]
[h3]Bosses[/h3]

Combat is also a key challenge in the player’s progression. To advance in the gang, the player must not only earn the respect of other members at their level but also[b] defeat a gang member who ranks above them[/b] in the hierarchy. It's a test of strength, survival of the fittest. This is where discovering the strengths and weaknesses of other prisoners comes in handy for the second time. Learning these helps us prepare for the fight against a mini-boss, such as prisoners from higher tiers. The enemy doesn’t like being pushed around? Then I’ll take knuckles with [i]Push to the fight[/i]. Does the enemy use shivs? I’ll bring extra bandages to prevent bleeding from their knives. Weak lungs? I’ll bring an extra toxic grenade.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/2eef8e3a5efce058b91931b02674ea9eea792e4d.gif[/img]

Combining all these systems and making the combat simple and fast while still maintaining depth was not an easy task. A key element was the introduction of preparation—discovering the strengths and weaknesses of the enemy, assembling the right party, and finally equipping them with the appropriate gear crafted on illegal workbenches.

The prisoners themselves, umm... I mean the players, played a crucial role in shaping how our combat system ultimately turned out. They provided incredibly valuable feedback, helping us refine the elements that mattered most to them and for that, we are super grateful!

Hope you enjoyed this reminder of the prison safety rules regarding engaging with other inmates and illegal activities such as contraband and fighting among prisoners.

Stay tuned for the upcoming news about the game!

See you behind bars!
Wooden Alien Team

notes.title: Dev Journal #7 - RPG mechanics
notes.content:
Hello there inmates,

We are super happy to be part of the Steam Turn-Based RPG Fest with a[b] -20% discount[/b] from today until October 7th! Come celebrate this amazing event with tons of game combining both turn-based mechanics and RPG aspects!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/5efcdda1c00b588733584de52a54153b47d33926.png[/img]
To accompany this event, here is our latest devblog where we will dig further into how we gave life to the secluded and dangerous world of an intergalactic prison and characters that shape the narrative of your sentence.

[h3]Creating an atmosphere[/h3]

One of the first things we knew when we began working on Space Prison was that we wanted to give players[b] the fantasy of being locked with quirky alien criminals.[/b] The RPG element was sort of implied in this fantasy - meeting the convicts, learning their stories, choosing who to befriend and who to fight.
So we implemented gangs as prison factions, and, within them, a relationship system where you can build relations with every inmate in the prison and a few features that support it: quest system, gifts, encounters etc... Quests are the main way of getting other convicts on your side, but you can also find other ways to do that.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/95e496f4d7272a6852c9af38c80f85cd2d611093.gif[/img]

Space prison is a very potent ground for making a unique RPG featuring things that are possible only in this setting. It translates flawlessly into mechanics like prison gangs, gaining convicts’ respect, challenging other inmates for their place in the hierarchy, crafting contraband items etc.

[h3]RPG mechanics: to embody and to socialize[/h3]

The goal of the player character is to escape the prison and to do that they need to survive first and climb up the prison social ladder. In short - join one of the gangs and advance to the top. BUT every player has their own story and their own path through the prison. 

To advance you need a certain amount of Respect from your peers. You get the Respect by completing their personal quest storylines. Therefore you choose which convicts to befriend and gain their respect and which ones to fight to advance in the gang hierarchy. And that’s on top of the gang that you choose. So to learn all the inmates and their stories you’d need to play through the game at least 4 times.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/4a72c3edd0da6860a655caf0d09b535ef5f07788.gif[/img]

Working on the alien criminal characters was one of the most fun processes in making Space Prison. We wanted to make quirky criminals that are tough, but at the same time original and interesting. So each one is really unique with their story, their looks, the way they speak and so on. The setting is so potent in terms of what you can come up with. Here sky even isn’t a limit. So as an example, we have a space pirate with an identity crisis that’s looking for their new crew, an investigative journalist, etc...

All these characters were created by the cooperation between the narrative team, the art team and the design team. Some of their stories reference popular themes or structures like Rocky or Groundhog Day and we have a ton of pop cultural references with subtle winks at all types of geeks. Players should have a lot of fun finding references to their favorite movies, books, comics or games.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/b27689296e497b257484e75b9483175f264e6c68.gif[/img]

[h3]Combat as a prison-themed interaction[/h3]

Designing combat was really fun. We wanted to use this notion that weapons are a contraband, so there’s scarcity of tools to fight with. Gathering resources is a first step of preparing for combat. The second one is crafting - at the beginning you craft makeshift weapons, armors and usable items, but later on when you get your hands on more high-end workbenches you craft real beauties like battle drones that become your party members and exchangeable parts for them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/4c58f925f99bba935a5ac0a176ad85a237231e8a.gif[/img]

We also wanted to relay this experience of prison being a closed space, so we made the combat arenas claustrophobic. We used a grid base but limited its space, so positioning in this tight space and using the environment makes it more interesting.

There are two main types of combat in the prison. A regular combat with alien creatures infesting the station and with weaker inmates. And more challenging fights with gang members. These are mini-boss fights that you need to prepare too. Each gang member has their weapons and armors they fight with along with a set of special strengths, weaknesses and statistics. To learn them you need to uncover them by getting information. This is a preparation part of the combat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/9783995ab4bbd243863df2babcdc660df78fbd4e.gif[/img]

Have fun during the event and try not to stir too much fight with other inmates (yes please do). Do not hesitate to leave us a review if you have not done it already or give some suggestions and feedback on the game. We will read them with pleasure! 

Stay tuned for more insights and future events to cell-ebrate!

See you behind bars!
Wooden Alien Team

notes.title: Devblog #6 - Survival mechanics
notes.content:
Hey inmates,

Today's devblog, we will talk further about what inspired our game and how we challenge ourselves with the idea of creating a survival game in a place as confined and strict as a prison.

[h3]Why a prison survival game?[/h3]

We wanted to make a space prison game from the start. We didn’t have a precise genre specified at the beginning, but survival mechanics made a lot of sense in a place like this. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/bd0a274977f5cb1aa6331556b4f9d93aa9a89032.gif[/img]

We needed to give them a twist though as the situation of the player character is far different than in most survival games. You are not stranded on an island/ocean/planet/forest and your main threats don’t come from the environment, flora and fauna. On the contrary, you are surrounded by other people (and aliens)... however[b] they are the main threat [/b]here. We needed to turn the systems so they reflect this[b] social survival aspect[/b] through the Relations with other inmates, the gang hierarchy, doing favors, gifts and so on...

[h3]Inspirations[/h3]

We were of course analyzing the rich history of movies, series and games about prisons, but our main inspirations were [i]Guardians of the Galaxy[/i], especially the scene in prison, and [i]Orange is the New Black[/i]. This series showed us how perspective changes when your freedom is limited and how many amazing stories can be told in a lockdown.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/a5ab145c2dd731e35711f7665f7929bdc790d2a7.gif[/img]

One of the major difficulty was to create a place where players were to be limited, but at the same time have an agency of their lives in prison. This is a challenge for most games – to make the repeatable game loop entertaining. We might have had an edge on this one as if anyone felt that the days in prison are getting a bit repetitive, they sometimes explained it to themselves that it’s how it goes down in prison.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/0dec07d4ec2adbeb4dbd735ba1f361411c57a7cd.gif[/img]

Yet, there is a lot of unique content in the game with [b]18 crafted and interesting gang inmates[/b], each with an original story that you can learn by doing their individual quest chains. From the beginning, we wanted to have a colorful cast of criminal characters.

[h3]Hope as a mechanic[/h3]

From a narrative perspective, it made a lot of sense to add a resource of Hope as in a grim and dangerous place like a remote jail, where you are sentenced to imprisonment sometimes longer than your lifetime, [b]hope is one of the most important resources[/b].

From a mechanic standpoint, we needed another resource that would balance Hunger and Health, so players could trade and balance these three, somewhat like Health, Hunger and Sanity in [i]Don’t Starve[/i]. Hope was perfect for it with low and high thresholds reflecting hopelessness or hopefulness in character’s statistics.

[h3]A survival game in a prison[/h3]

It was a challenge as survivals are known for their open worlds. Prison’s idea is that it limits the inmates freedoms, one of which is the freedom of space and movement. That’s why we needed to get creative. We went more in the direction of a wild prison with simple rules. Think more [i]Riddick [/i]or [i]Alien 3[/i] than [i]Shawshank Redemption[/i].

To make the space more interesting we divided it into [b]biomes[/b]. We also divided it into locations that are available for inmates and those that are restricted, like labs, engine or control rooms, that also feed the grim narrative of the prison.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/3268b6f21684678b2930ff52e6bd893b37720cdd.gif[/img]

Furthermore, we needed to keep exploring the locations everyday fresh for players, so we came up with the idea of [b]moving corridors[/b]. The prison map changes everyday, because the space station is designed in a way that the corridors move, disabling convicts from planning an escape. After all, you're sentenced here forever, right?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/1c810a8f61df97578d7c5665cbc4e076817296c9.gif[/img]

Thank you all for your support and the heartwarming feedback you gave on the release of the game. We read all your suggestions and enthusiasm about the life in Space Prison with great pleasure and feel free to leave us a review if you have not done it already!

Stay tuned for more insights as we continue to work on adding new content to Space Prison!

See you behind bars!
Wooden Alien Team

notes.title: Release details and a word from the team!
notes.content:
Hey inmates!

The release is closing in, and you’ve got questions about the big day on July 18! Here are the answers you’re hunting for! Space Prison will launch during TactiCon and will be showcased from July 18 to July 22!

[i]Please note that the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1865930/view/4161970072171156587]previous Steam news article[/url] incorrectly stated the [b]release time[/b] for Space Prison; the correct starting hour is [b]8:00 PM (CEST)[/b] instead of 4:00 PM (CEST).[/i] We've made a [b]release timing map[/b] further below in this post!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/81e8314dbef76211f4cc4b85f5da6ff44f833ca2.png[/img]

But, first off, the whole team wanted to share a word with you:

We just wanted to take this occasion to say a huge [b]THANK YOU[/b] to all of you who've been testing our game and providing us with your invaluable feedback. Your input has been crucial in making Space Prison the game it is today.

Thanks to you, we've been able to fine-tune the gameplay, squash bugs, and add features that make the game even more exciting and engaging. Because of your feedback, we were able to focus on the things that really matter to you, like cool criminal characters, turn-based combat and, of course, space rats. We couldn't have done it without you!

For those of you looking to buy Space Prison, we wanted to clear up a couple of things about what the game isn't:
[list]
[*] It’s NOT a roguelike (nor a roguelite). While we do have roguelite elements like a prison map that changes every day (corridors shift, so prisoners can’t plan their escape) and player character dying, you do not need to start from scratch when you snuff it. Your consciousness is saved in the collar and transferred to a new body (“Death is not an excuse for a shorter sentence”).
[*] It’s not The Escapists. While you do plan your survival and interactions, Space Prison is more about doing quests for quirky criminals to get them to join your squad, challenging others for their spot in the gang, gathering and gearing up your party to use them in turn-based combat against other inmates, alien creatures infesting the station and prison system itself.
[*] It’s not a Space Rat Breeding Simulator. Even though, thanks to you guys, we’ve added many improvements for the rats (naming them, equipping them with tiny weapons for battle, healing them in your cell's burrow or upgrading their skills), we’re not a game about raising space rats;)
[/list]
So, if you're ready for a wild ride in the galaxy's most notorious prison, filled with tactical combat, social RPG mechanics, and a whole lot of space rats, then Space Prison is the game for you.
Thanks again for all your support and feedback. We can't wait to see you behind bars!

Cheers!

_

notes.title: Dev Journal #5 - Map & Corridors
notes.content:
Hey inmates,

In today's devblog, we're coming back to the making of the map, the prison corridors, and the environments, where every day brings its share of new challenges and opportunities for exploration.

[h2]Mix of procedurally generated & handcrafted[/h2]

When creating the first concept of Space Prison, we rapidly chose an [b]ever-changing map[/b] where we blend procedurally generated corridors with a series of fully handcrafted environments. What do we mean by that? The [b]prison's heart[/b] is the [b]cellblock[/b], from where you can go to [b]Locations[/b] like the Medical Bay, the Dining Hall, or the Bathroom, and even further once you get restricted access cards. But to get to any of the locations, you will have to cross the corridors with pathways broken into nodes, which lead to rooms.

[h3]Corridors evolving daily[/h3]
Each day, you have a [b]new set of corridors[/b] connecting each location with a selection of rooms that can hide combat encounters, events with characters, guard patrols, special objects, or loot. You will never enter the same rooms in the same order. All the rooms are manually designed and drawn. We have very talented artists that create beautiful 2D stylized art.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/01bdc8867c98b045aef473dc5bd13f07eef10baf.png[/img]

[h3]Hand-drawn environments[/h3]
We’re aware that today AI can make great artwork that can sometimes be indistinguishable from human-made art, but we believe it cannot provide seamless locations, not to mention locations that blend with each other seamlessly. And there’s still something unmatched in the [b]hand-made art[/b]. That’s why we decided to make the assets, the level design, and the level art ourselves. But as we still wanted to get you something fresh every day by designing the corridors of the prison to shift every day, so the prisoners couldn’t plan their escape.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/dbe86242b2d8ab74612285a1afea733a9cfbd153.jpg[/img]


[h2]Making a "closed-world"[/h2]

At the very beginning of the development, we were actually considering and experimenting with making a “closed-world survival” as opposed to popular open-world survivals. And back in the early prototypes, the prison was much more closed and claustrophobic. However, when we started running the first playtests with our community, it was obvious that we needed to give them [b]more space for exploration[/b], as in a proper survival game. In order to accomplish this, we did two things:
[list]
[*] Added the [b]procedurally generated corridors[/b]. They change every day to keep inmates from planning the escape.
[*] Divided the facility into the [b]Inner Ring[/b] and [b]Outer Ring[/b]. The Inner Ring has locations like Dining Hall, Bathroom, or Medical Bay, which prisoners are allowed to access. And the Outer Ring is out of bounds for inmates because there are Engine Rooms, Power Hubs, or Labs there. In order to get there, you need to get a special keycard, and even then, you need to be careful not to step on a guard patrol.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/b2525d19848379003139730a5341d1a0b489f320.png[/img]


[h2]Designing the prison[/h2]

When making the map and each individual area, we made sure that each location was designed to best [b]reflect its real function[/b]. So the Dining Hall, for example, has some tables, a window where the food is being sold (yeah, you need to pay for chow in this place), or windows where you can sell creature meat that you hunt in the corridors (that will most probably be made into tomorrow’s dinner). But it also has braziers where you can cook the meat yourself, a Kitchen area that is out of bounds for inmates but that you can break into to steal ingredients or cook better meals, and of course, a scanner that keeps you from getting in our out with a shiv (or at least that’s supposed to be doing).

On top of that, we decided to add a [b]pool of conditions[/b] from which one is randomly selected by the game at the beginning of a new day. An area can be closed temporarily, a bonus or penalty can be applied for combat, relationship gains, etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/3eb84d84e895971c6d54044e3fa307e7de37a9f6.png[/img]


[h2]Our creative process[/h2]

We designed the prison facility as a [b]circle[/b], because what’s a better closed shape than a circle? The prisoners are supposed to keep themselves to the Inner Ring, so they are closed even more tightly with the whole Outer Ring region, which is patrolled heavily by guards, guard dogs, and drones.
Exploration in this place is not only about knowing where the guards are. When you venture into the corridor labyrinth, you need to come prepared. There are many dangerous creatures roaming this station. Location areas are a bit civilized (if you can call it that with the galaxy's most notorious criminals in there), but corridors are like a wild west—no one really cares what happens to prisoners, so you can meet every kind of disgusting creature you can think of (yeah, Baby Wyrsts too).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/432c664b3e1cdeb341b5c5e866607212b6b94b6d.gif[/img]

But sometimes even the nastiest creatures are better than a Ferath assassin waiting for you with their company because you haven’t brought them the dinner they tried to extort from you. Good thing is that you can deal with situations like this in a few ways. You can, for example, be a good boy or girl and bring them what they want. But if you don’t want to be considered a pushover for the rest of your sentence, you can also choose the tough inmates that fit your party, get on their good side, and befriend them so they can cover your back when you need it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/af2e8b808885ca113a6982f036937db974b68643.gif[/img]

Thank you all for your support and for participating in our demos and playtests. Your feedback is always incredibly precious in helping us continuously improve the game.

Stay tuned for more insights as we continue to advance the development of Space Prison!

See you behind bars!
Wooden Alien Team

notes.title: Dev Journal #3 - Player-Based Changes
notes.content:
Hey inmates!

It's time for another update on the developments within the confines of Space Prison. We've been hard at work incorporating your [b]feedback and suggestions[/b] to improve your experience within our facility. We wanted to let you know the [b]biggest changes[/b] made since the Steam Next Fest demo, the various playtests we held, and our latest demo this year!

[h3]Before we start, your opinion is important to us, so feel free to [b]share your ideas and suggestions[/b] with our [b][url=https://spaceprison.featureupvote.com/?order=new&filter=all&tag=]upvoting tool[/url][/b]! We take all your feedback into consideration, thank you for your commitment![/h3]

[url=https://spaceprison.featureupvote.com/?order=top&filter=all&tag=][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/bf89d0eabe0613fb9b7ab9b95a571c4420b71e9c.png[/img][/url]
[i]As you can see, the rats are very popular![/i]


[h2]Tactical depth[/h2]

[h3]Hazards and obstacles[/h3]
Thanks to your requests, we’ve added a [b]new feature[/b] for combat encounters for more tactical depth during fights. Say hello to [b]hazards and obstacles[/b]! Combat arenas along the prison have objects that can be dangerous for you, but that you can use to your advantage if you play around them smartly. Exploit the terrain strategically to your advantage and fight your way out with more diversity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/0fceb018f126268ae9cbfafd89e543912408c59c.gif[/img]

[h3]Party member loadout management[/h3]
Your fellow rats and allies are now [b]fully manageable[/b] in one convenient location: the [b]party menu[/b]. Equip them with different [b]gear[/b] depending on how you want to play. From weapons and armor to specialized combat items, equip your companions with the tools they need to be your partners in crime! Oh, even the rats have their own gear with Tiny Knuckles or Rat Capes [i](yes, they wear their dead comrades as armor, that's a thing)[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/4ed1505bfadbf25fe29da306b7e62b81d52313c2.gif[/img]

[h2]Rat healing mechanic[/h2]
We know you formed a special bond with your rodent companions, we all do! Because you requested to be able to keep them longer and care for them, rats can now [b]heal during the night[/b]. But why stop there? We're working on a [b]dedicated area[/b] within your cell equipped with cozy [b]beds for your rat[/b] friends.

[h2]Outer ring exploration[/h2]
Want to explore beyond the familiar corners of your cell? We've added a whole new part of the prison that is [b]restricted to inmates[/b], with [b]new locations[/b] like Labs, Power Hub, or the out-of-order Prison Yard. You need to get a [b]special keycard[/b] to get there. And even if you do, you need to be extra careful, as you will be attacked at sight by merciless guards, drones, and guard dogs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/8e19846eac04d5aaa1396757c00d64135ca7b82f.png[/img]

[h2]Adding a second gang[/h2]
Fulfilling a long-awaited request from the community, you will have the freedom to [b]choose between two gangs[/b] and explore the [b]unique narratives[/b] and [b]quests[/b] offered by each faction and its members. So, that means you’ll have twice as many interesting NPCs with their own stories and chain quests to discover, depending on your run! (And a special gang hideout for each gang!)

[h3]Other important changes made since the Steam Next Fest Demo and playtests:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Animations:[/b] Following your feedback during the Steam Next Fest demo, we've reworked the NPC and environmental animations to make them more impactful and smoother.
[*] [b]Sound Design:[/b] You outlined the room for improvement of Space Prison music and sound design, and that is why we heard you (get it), you can listen to some of the changes in this [url=https://www.facebook.com/WoodenAlienGames/videos/750022363712832]video[/url]. We have also added new sounds for our NPCs. Music is an important topic for us as well, and we're exploring the musical atmosphere of the game. We shared one of our experiments [url=https://discord.com/channels/1092181800979288236/1092481642741907476/1197940293484417164]on our Discord[/url]!
[*] [b]Storyline & lore:[/b] You suggested that it would be nice to learn more about the Space Prison and have more lore to discover throughout the game. So, we focused on expanding it by creating unique race and crime backgrounds for NPCs, and more. Get a glimpse of the Space Prison lore in our previous [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1865930/view/7251430632280177989]Devblog[/url].[/list] https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1865930/view/7251430632280177989
[list] [*] [b]Combat balancing:[/b] Since the first public demo feedback, we have worked more on balancing out the combat and making it more interesting for you. Gear, including weapons and usable items, are not the only additions, we also implemented new abilities and created new and varied enemies.
[*] [b]Difficulty:[/b] The Space Prison is a tough place, but some of the areas seemed either a little too harsh or too easy, from what we understood after reading your comments. That is why we worked especially hard on evening them out. Based on the latest playtests and the demo, the difficulty was better handled. We'll keep on balancing the game so that it remains a challenging experience but is still approachable for the new fishes in the tank.
[*] [b]Tutorials:[/b] Some of you felt lost at times and requested more explanation of various game mechanics. We added new tutorials and improved some of the previous ones. Recently, we had some new ideas for in-game information display, we are currently working on improving the information system even further.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/7f6827c4a218eed59e4e86340e6dcf9a3fc7a74e.gif[/img]

We thank you all for taking part of this journey and participating in our demos and playtests. The [b]feedback[/b] you provide is invaluable to help us in the continuous improvement of the game. Your voices [b]shape the experience[/b] of Space Prison, and we're committed to delivering the best one possible!

Stay tuned for more updates as we continue to develop Space Prison!

See you behind bars!
Wooden Alien Team

notes.title: Dev Journal #2 - Setting and playable races
notes.content:
Hey inmates,

In today’s post, we'll explore further three key aspects of the game: the [b]setting[/b] of the Space Prison itself, the [b]playable races[/b] within it, and the [b]crimes[/b] you committed.

[h2]The Space Prison setting[/h2]

Space Prison is not your average hellhole. It's an [b]experimental penitentiary[/b] located on a space station, housing the most notorious criminals from across the galaxy. Imagine being locked up—truly guilty or not—in a huge metal can with inhumane living conditions, vicious alien creatures, tough convicts, and sadistic guards. Will you survive? Will you rise in the gang hierarchy, or have the will to attempt a daring escape? Only one person has managed to pull that out before. Supposedly.

The game features a [b]colorful cast of criminals[/b], each with their own personal quest chain; survival mechanics like crafting and building up your prison cell; turn-based brawls for setting up arguments and a bunch of roguelite elements. But why a Space Prison, you may ask. Four years ago, when we sat at a drawing board, we already knew what kind of games we wanted to make. We strive to make distinct titles—games that offer an experience and atmosphere that no other games do. We didn’t want to make another fantasy RPG or Souls-like. From all the ideas we had, Space Prison was an obvious choice—its [b]distinct setting[/b], [b]mechanics[/b], and [b]art style[/b] make it a unique and fun experience.

And for rest? Well, we’ll keep the mystery so you can enjoy it yourself!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/8eded9d3e955ac9862893bbb0d6b7b65ed81ea3a.png[/img]


[h2]The playable races[/h2]

In Space Prison, you can choose from [b]three distinct races[/b], each with its own background, abilities, and playstyle. We needed them to differ so strongly that it would be easy to assign various skills, perks, and stats to them. Why three races? Because three is the magic number! In all seriousness, if you get locked in Space Prison, you will see that in the game we have over a dozen various alien races. We selected the three that we believe to be the most distinct and appealing as playable races.

The races were definitely the team’s joint effort. They were born with the vision of our art team, who designed them visually. When we had these distinct and interesting looking races, then our narration and design team took them under their care to make them distinct from each other and other races we have in the game. We added their [b]backgrounds[/b] and set them apart for [b]different playstyles[/b]. What’s very important to us, we didn’t want any race (or sex for that matter) to define any of the characters. That’s why, even though they have distinct backgrounds, you can see that all of them have equal chances to become any type of criminal they want.
[i]We're very interested in finding out which alien races you will like the most. Although I must admit that “muscle alien ladies” already have an impressive fanbase.[/i]

Now, without further ado, let’s take a look at these big baddies:

[h3]Ferath[/h3]
Feraths are on the verge of extinction after a gene mutation entwined a life-threatening disease with the chromosome Y. There are few male individuals left in the universe, and they are imprisoned on Ferra (their origin planet) and forced to reproduce as much as possible with selected female Ferraths, to produce more boys. They are known for having one horn, fur on their torsos and hands, and a large tail. Some of them believe that their predecessors were the infamous, [b]intergalactic Yetis[/b], [i]but the theory has never been confirmed[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/dc0cfc06d513eadb1cc9e8ba38f07a92dbd4c975.png[/img]

[h3]Nex[/h3]
Nex are [b]cyborgs[/b] from the Nexus galaxy that are actively looking for their Inventor and answers regarding the ‘how’ and ‘why’ they were created. They undergo physical transformations to imitate their prophet, who rejected a biological body for a cybernetic one. Her reasons for doing that are unknown, because there is scarcely any knowledge left from the time she lived. Nex have cellular bodies merged with artificial parts. They modify their organisms and use various enhancements to reach individual goals. The enhancements are fueled by a special substance - one that is very efficient, however very scarce in the Nexus galaxy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/6c697d45975af18f421a6b37cba92ef146d4940e.png[/img]

[h3]Human[/h3]
Ah, the good ol’  [b]typical biped mammal[/b] that we all are! The human race has finally reached technological advancement, allowing them to travel between different galaxies in the universe. When they had first crawled out of the Milky Way, they started to rapidly expand their territory and appear all over the universe. Thus, some alien races began to think of them as lower evolutionary species, hardly resilient on their own, but stronger in packs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/7ba78d8b97700b85291c667747817334bec1eafb.png[/img]

[h2]The crimes[/h2]

In Space Prison, every character has their own criminal background, determining their skills and challenges.

[h3]Smuggler[/h3]
Smugglers are experts in the art of concealment. They are skilled in hiding contraband and avoiding inspections, however they are sometimes too slow on their feet.
[list]
[*] Secret Pockets - You start your sentence with one contraband item smuggled in
[*] Slow Reflexes - Takes 50% more damage from hazards
[/list]
[h3]Assassin[/h3]
Assassins believe their bodies are living weapons. They rely on the momentum of their movements to kill their targets. Unsurprisingly, this way of life comes with a grim outlook on the world.
[list]
[*] Deadly Maneuvers - After Moving: Next Attack +30% damage, Duration: Infinite
[*] Fatalist - Hope Gain: Decreased by -20%
[/list]
[h3]Saboteur[/h3]
Saboteurs use rats and other goons to wreak havoc on their targets. They believe in strength in numbers and that life is expandable. As a result, freelancers charge them higher fees.
[list]
[*] Give all your rats additional combat slots
[*] Fodders Hire Price: Increased by 50%
[/list]
[h3]Thief[/h3]
Driven by greed and the prospect of easy money, they employ their talents to steal credits and valuable artifacts. People know not to trust them with their possessions, that is why it’s hard for them to form any kind of business relations.
[list]
[*] Meticulous - Has 100% chance of double loot from Loot Boxes
[*] Relation Gain: -10%
[/list]
[h3]Con Artist[/h3]
Con Artists are criminals who make their living out of deception. They know how to put up a facade in front of others, but are less resilient to physical harm.
[list]
[*] Relation Gain: +20%
[*] Feeble: Damage +20%
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/1df530e6fb6e16332895a7dba557bd3dbccfcd67.png[/img]

Each crime offers [b]unique bonuses and challenges[/b], allowing you to choose the kind of criminal you want to be and customize your experience in the Space Prison.

With Space Prison, we want to create a thrilling blend of survival, strategy, and storytelling in a unique setting. Stay tuned for more updates as we continue to develop Space Prison (and the Early Access release is fast approaching already)!

See you behind bars!
Wooden Alien Team

notes.title: Dev Journal #1 - Expanding the Space Prison
notes.content:
Hey inmates,

In the darkest corners of the Space Prison, we’ve been working hard to make sure that you’ll have a “pleasant” stay at the prison. NPCs, quests, gang hierarchy, guards, objects, UI, and so on. Let’s review all of this together, shall we?

It was quite busy on our end with the [b]design of a stage of progression[/b], addition of [b]new quests[/b], economy, prison [b]locations[/b] and [b]sublocations[/b], corridors, [b]combat[/b] encounters, and improvement of the game and features [b]based on the feedback[/b] you gave us.

[h2]New playable race![/h2]
Meet the [b]Ferath[/b]—evolution's brawny marvels. It’s the face of the game in the key art, a big horned muscular alien. Menacing and ferocious, but also swift and powerful. They close in on enemies quickly to unleash their violence in a close-and-personal fashion. A perfect fit for the unforgiving confines of Space Prison.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/1d36f531d523defd1257c8027d40aabb03b96224.jpg[/img]
[h3]UI and sound effects[/h3]
We're continuously [b]improving and streamlining the UI[/b] to make sure that you have a clear and smooth onboarding process. We’ve added item categories and inventory slots for them, like Weapons, Armors, and Combat Usables. On top of that, [url=https://twitter.com/Wooden_Alien/status/1751983537614631392][b]many new sounds[/b][/url] were added or improved, and we’re also working on the [b]soundtrack[/b] of the game, as we shared on social media. The sound design, but the music in particular, is still [b]experimental[/b]. So we welcome your feedback on it!

[h3]Hirelings and rats, trusty companions[/h3]
As part of the UI process, you now both have your [b]rats and allies grouped in a "Party" screen[/b]. You can see their stats, but you can also customize their gear, changing the way they help you in combat. We’ve also upgraded the Rat Nest in Player Cell. Taming rats is not the only thing you can do now, you can craft items for them, from snacks to special tiny rat weapons. Aren’t they just adorable with their little gear? Finally, we’ve added a [b]new crime[/b], Saboteur, which has [b]advantages in rat management[/b].



[h2]Death is no excuse for a shorter sentence[/h2]

[h3]New death, new you[/h3]
Remember what the guards said? You can forget about resting in peace. Death is just a temporary inconvenience in our necks (ha, get it, collars, necks). No matter how hard you try, as long as your collar remains intact, you'll be brought back, and yours never seems to have a crack. Well, [b]partially brought back[/b] to be exact, we can't replicate your body, so you'll have to choose and work with another meat sack among a [b]selection of random race and crime specializations[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/f5a07f1437924ed9a3d43ceee3cb6ec8be24ad42.png[/img]
[h3]Permadeath mode[/h3]
Well, you can spice things up by having a [b]faulty collar[/b], meaning there’s no bringing you back this time. Try your luck next time with the permadeath mode and see how long you last in the dog-eat-dog world of the Space Prison. Your body's organic waste may or may not be turned into dinner if you don't make it.



[h2]More variety in quests[/h2]
NPCs and the story mean a lot to us. The game has become [b]much richer in mechanics and content[/b] than we expected. You will have a lot to do and discover, and there is no time to stay idle. But the amount of content we added made us feel like it could be overwhelming. We came to the conclusion that it needed to be [b]more spread out in time and space[/b] so that you could discover new quests, locations, and items at a smoother pace. This led to a more clearly segmented progression with [b]better onboarding[/b] in order to let you get the hang of it all. We also implemented the quests to join the Hypernova and Gravity Fists gangs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/ee92d24ef5766010c747014d649344b9dd3f31e2.jpg[/img]
[h3]Quest chains[/h3]
We have been focusing on quests lately by adding quest chains linked to members of the gang you joined. They'll let you [b]discover more about your fellow inmates[/b] and gang members. We are still implementing these quests, so more are on the way. We focus on and pride ourselves on [b]crafting handmade and interesting convicts[/b] with their own backgrounds and personal stories about their time in prison. You can learn about them if you decide to befriend and help them. NPCs alone would deserve a proper devblog about them, so expect one in the future!

[h3]Threat quests[/h3]
To reinforce the gang mechanics and the impact of choosing one gang over another, we added the "threat quests". The [b]opposing gangs will hold a grudge[/b] against you and try to intimidate you, or worse.

[h3]Universal jobs[/h3]
Need a little extra cash to gather resources, grease the wheels of justice, or hire inmates? As part of our quest process, we have been crafting a system for making [b]procedurally-generated quests[/b]. So there will be more than enough quests to keep you busy between shakedowns!


[h2]Exploration and fast travel[/h2]
Exploration is a big part of the game. You shared that there was a lot of coming back and forth before. We iterated and found a solution: [b]resize some locations[/b], rework the [b]pathing[/b], and add a shortcut to the gang hub in the cell on top of the waypoints for [b]fast travel[/b].

[h3]Waypoints[/h3]
Tattooing your plan for escape and the prison map on your body is pointless here. The architect of the prison has crafted the prison so that the [b]corridors are rearranged every day[/b] to make sure that you won't make it out. But there is something else that you can do: build secret [b]teleporters[/b] and [b]hidden pathways[/b]. Shave precious minutes off your sentence with these fast travel shortcuts. Just don't let the guards get wind of your little detours.

[h3]More locations[/h3]
The Space Prison is expanding! Venture beyond the confines of your cell and your regular corridors. You will be able to explore the [b]outer ring[/b] of the prison. We've added [b]3 new locations[/b] with their own set of [b]sublocations[/b] and more corridors. From the yard to the science lab to the power hub, there's a whole new segment of the prison to sneak into. But beware! The second ring is strictly forbidden to inmates. Don’t let the guards see you wandering there, or you’ll wish that you’d been in the vacuum of space instead. It would be more merciful than what they plan for you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/3b008bf5b8db55143f681c35164083ac0179af11.png[/img]
[h3]Combat arenas[/h3]
We've been adding more variety and life to the environments with animated elements. Get ready to duke it out in style there. Just don't get too distracted by the scenery, or you might end up on the wrong end of a fist.



[h2]Salvaging, gear durability, and collectibles[/h2]
Based on your input, we [b]emphasized the survival aspect[/b] of the gear, which has a [b]durability gauge[/b] and can be repaired or salvaged.

[h3]Repair system, weapon and armor durability[/h3]
If your gear's looking torn or broken, then you might as well have a target on your back, those fists ain't going to help even if you’re built like one of 'em Feraths. Swing by a [b]repair station[/b] that we designed and patch things up before the next brawl, trust me, you'll need it. Because nothing says "dead person walking" like a broken shiv.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/58a1820a428f3230536002f9853cd710ae839e33.png[/img]
[h3]Processing stations[/h3]
A new addition to your prison survival handbook! From base materials to top-tier contraband, this feature has you covered. [b]Process tier 1 materials[/b] into tier 2 ones, or the other way around, to [b]salvage resources[/b]. Just remember to keep a low profile, weapons are prohibited.

[h3]Collectibles[/h3]
We're crafting collectible comic strips, a small form of entertainment for you, inmates, to read in peace in your cell.

[h3]Giving & buying item systems[/h3]
Regarding the buying system, each of your gang mates has a specific list of items they can trade with you. You can learn about these items by uncovering information on them with an Intel resource. As for the giving mechanic, we changed how it works. Before, each inmate wanted one specific item. Now you can experiment with what they will accept, and some items will improve your relations with them better than others.



[h2]A less welcoming prison[/h2]
We heard your feedback about the combat system. Our main goal is to motivate you to [b]change tactics[/b] by facing a wider range of enemies and hazards. By reworking the combat system and enemies, we decided to add [b]more encounters[/b] and limit the number of the same possible encounters per day.

[h3]New mobs[/h3]
The prison is full of monsters, and no, I'm not only talking about alien inmates or Bob. There are creatures lurking in the corridors, rival gangs, guards, and prisoners are not the only ones you need to keep an eye on. We've been designing and adding a handful of enemies, and we're not done yet!

[h3]Gang members as mini-bosses[/h3]
Speaking of gang members, they are more than your regular low-key prisoners now. Gang members aren't just small fries. They're [b]mini-bosses[/b], and that means that you have to prepare yourself for these battles. You should use [b]Intel to uncover information[/b] on the convicts you will fight with to prepare better. Time to sharpen those improvised brass knuckles and beef up your rat companions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/ce078ddabd2df6d85ab9dab95e15c9d227e34155.jpg[/img]
[h3]Hazards and traps[/h3]
Who said traps are just for others to use? We decided to add [b]more diversity to the fights[/b] with hazards and traps. As part of that decision, we've added this feature so that you and your party can arm yourself with traps to ease your wrists with all that fighting. With every fight comes its share of uncertainty and unanticipated hazards. Watch out for them, they are dangerous for you too, but there can also be [b]special hazard loot crates[/b] during combat.



Phew, as you can see, we've been busy working on new content and polishing what you reported. It was a big devblog, but don't worry, now you're up-to-speed! Thank you for your feedback, it's like the prison chef's special burger after a good brawl: precious and thrilling. Until next time, stay out of trouble, fish, and get your hands on the prison newspaper for more information on the development process.

See you behind bars!
Wooden Alien Team

notes.title: DEMO 2.0 AVAILABLE NOW!
notes.content:
Oh, boy, have we got a lot for you in this [b]brand new demo[/b]! 

We have read your appeals, convicts, and we've decided to grant you some of your major requests in this Demo 2.0. Only for good behavior, mind you. But don't think that it's a rule! 👮

Here are just a few things we’ve added lately:
[olist]
[*] [b]A new playable race - Ferath[/b]. Responding to the appeals of Space Prison convicts, we're excited to introduce a thrilling addition: the ability to embody your beloved muscular alien lady.
[*] [b]Hazards and Obstacles[/b]. Combat arenas now contain dangerous objects that can be a hazard for your party. But you can also use them to your advantage, if you play around them smartly.
[*] [b]Special Rat Items[/b]. We’ve upgraded the Rat Nest in player Cell. Now you can invest resources into enhancing your rat, transforming it into a reliable ally and your ultimate friend.
[*] [b]Party Screen[/b]. All your allies in one place. You can see their stats and inventory and customize their gear changing the way they help you in combat.
[*] [b]Hypernova intro quest[/b]. You had a chance to prove yourself to Gravity Fist in the previosu demo. Now you can choose to join the Hypernova anarchists gang. If you’ve got the guts.
[*] [b]Saboteur[/b]. A new playable crime who uses Rat Tactics as their combat advantage.
[/olist]
Aaaaand much more fixes and improvements.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/dc19d9d6513690c895a0146f951d0739d73cb453.png[/img]

No need to hesitate – simply grab your keyboard and dive right into the action! But with caution. Remember - it's a Strategy Fest 😉

[h3]Brand New Demo is Awaiting!![/h3]

notes.title: DD Indie Showcase, Your Feedback & External Tests
notes.content:
[h3]Hello, Inmate[/h3]

It's been a while since our reveal, so it's time to share with you some news from the nastiest prison in the galaxy...

Somewhere in space: our developers gave an [url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/space-prison/interview][b]interview for PCGamsN[/b][/url], revealing some secrets about the darkest hole in the universe...

[h3]Among the finalists[/h3]

On May 15th and 16th, we had the opportunity to participate in [b]Digital Dragons[/b] which is one of the Europe's largest business events, addressed to the representatives of the digital entertainment sector. Space Prison was among [b]the finalists of Indie Showcase[/b] there. This event was also a great opportunity to show our game to a wider group of players and collect feedback.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/143ac5f4d5c34ee6c97006626570266dfe5dc82d.jpg[/img]
[h3]New key art[/h3]

It is [b]because of players' opinions, we decided to replace the Space Prison key art[/b], which you will see on our Steam page from now on. We also found out which elements and game mechanics of the game you like the most.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43798268/1b8957bde126870b7f706349393e84e1dbec0d7f.png[/img]

[h3]External tests[/h3]

Soon we plan to show our work to more players, so expect some good news n the near future. Those who would like to [b]participate in the testing process[/b] and be the first ones to escape from the Space Prison - please visit our [url=http://discord.com/invite/9aCaaZzZxj][b]Discord[/b][/url]. Among you, our community, we are planning to recruit our first group of testers for the new build of the game.

Thanks for being with us and see you soon!
